title.narrative: Activity under preparation Stabilisation efforts DRC-UG border

description.narrative: Contract related to: Stabilisation efforts DRC-UG border - Border regions across Sub-Saharan Africa are characterised by complex, overlapping dynamics of fragility, where weak governance, insecurity, displacement and migratory movements, and limited economic opportunities intersect with environmental degradation and demographic pressures. These cross-border settings often experience the spillover of conflict, violent extremism, and illicit trade, while remaining vital corridors for mobility, trade, and cooperation. Addressing these challenges requires integrated, conflict-sensitive approaches that combine security, governance, and socio-economic resilience.The Action takes an integrated approach connecting peace, security, governance, and sustainable development to address fragility stemming from governance deficits, resource pressures, demographic trends, and climate change across the targeted regions. It also tackles displacement and migratory challenges, contributing to the EU¿s migration agenda through stability, inclusion, and sustainable solutions in priority areas.The overall objective of this Action is to prevent and mitigate instability and the impact of local conflicts in border areas. This subject was identified in Priority Area 2 (Democratic Governance, Peace and Security, Culture), Specific Objective 2 (Peace and Security) of the Multi-Annual Indicative Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa 2021-2027. The Action is in line with SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions, as well as No poverty (SDG 1); Zero hunger (SDG 2); Reduce inequality (SDG 10), Gender equality (SDG 5), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8) and Climate action (SDG 13).The action will target four different geographical windows: (i) border areas between Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, and Guinea (West Africa window) which face structural weaknesses worsened by climate change and natural resources degradation trafficking, and violent extremism. In this region, the Action will aim to enhance stability and resilience in border areas through inclusive economic growth, sustainable resource management, and coordinated action against cross-border trafficking; (ii) border areas between Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) - Uganda (Great Lakes window), where armed groups, natural resource exploitation, and weak law enforcement shape regional dynamics. In this area, the Action will enhance stability and resilience by addressing the drivers of violent extremism and fostering inclusive socio-economic development; (iii) border areas between Kenya, Somalia, Ethiopia and South Sudan (Horn of Africa window), where climate change jeopardises the main economic activities thus worsening inter-communal and cross-border conflict. In this region, the Action will aim to enhance peace, resilience, and sustainable growth in cross-border communities (including those affected by displacement) through strengthened conflict management, sustainable natural resource use, and inclusive, climate-smart economic development; (iv) border areas between Malawi and Mozambique (Southern Africa window) impacted by radicalisation within vulnerable communities and the spill over of terrorism and organised crime. Here, the Action will enhance institutional cooperation and community resilience to prevent conflict and radicalisation, fostering inclusive and secure border environments.The Action will be carried out in complementarity and coordination with both EU and non-EU funded actions at national and regional level, including relevant Regional Economic Communities and other regional stakeholders. This would include relevant TEIs, nexus actions, green deal sector related actions, as well as actions addressing terrorism spillover.
